title: The Modified-Risk Claim and Charitable Rewards
lessons: An age-verified adult smoker receives ZYN marketing using the modified-risk claim FDA authorized for twenty classic ZYN products in June 2026.
The player opens the ZYN Rewards store and finds charitable donations listed beside merchandise and gift cards.

text: An age-verified adult smoker receives ZYN marketing using the modified-risk claim FDA authorized for twenty classic ZYN products in June 2026.

entry-first-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: I am required to read the claim as authorized: "Using ZYN instead of cigarettes puts you at a lower risk of mouth cancer, heart disease, lung cancer, stroke, emphysema, and chronic bronchitis."

entry-first-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: You listed six diseases before hello.

entry-first-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Hello.

entry-first-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: Is this the part where you say FDA approved?

entry-first-5.speaker: COUNSEL
text: No. FDA authorized specified products to be marketed with that claim. The agency expressly distinguishes marketing authorization from FDA approval and states that no tobacco product is safe.

choice-first.speaker: COUNSEL
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: If someone already smokes, relative-risk information is useful.
The words "instead of cigarettes" are doing a lot of work there.
I do not want a nicotine brand using disease risk as a sales message.

first-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The record will reflect that relative-risk information is material to you. For completeness, FDA states that fully quitting tobacco use provides the greatest health benefit.

first-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Correct. The authorized comparison is ZYN instead of cigarettes. It is not a blanket statement about every pattern of use.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: You looked happy saying "correct."

first-2-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Objection. Speculation.

first-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Authorization permits the claim. It does not compel you to find the claim persuasive or welcome in advertising.
The player opens the ZYN Rewards store and finds charitable donations listed beside merchandise and gift cards.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Why is "Donate to Hope For The Warriors" in the same store as an Amazon gift card and a metal can?

entry-return-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: We Care by ZYN permits Rewards members to direct points to participating charitable organizations. The brand states that donated points are valued at four cents each for this purpose.

entry-return-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: So my nicotine loyalty points become philanthropy.

entry-return-4.speaker: COUNSEL
text: In the quantities and organizations made available through the program, yes.

entry-return-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: And ZYN itself?

entry-return-6.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The company states a commitment of three million dollars annually to We Care by ZYN. Current featured organizations include groups serving veterans, active-duty service members, and their families.

choice-return.speaker: COUNSEL
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: If the points already exist, I would rather donate them than get another branded thing.
This is still cause marketing attached to a nicotine loyalty program.
I do not want charity used to make the purchase relationship feel better.

return-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Your points may be allocated accordingly. No branded hoodie is required.

return-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The charitable function and the brand benefit can coexist. One does not legally cancel the other.

return-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: You are not required to convert a commercial relationship into a moral one.

return-3-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: That was almost human.

return-3-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Please strike "almost" from the record.
